title: Implementing a Generative LDA Classifier from Scratch
description: Fit shared within-class covariance cov_, class means means_, and class priors priors_ in LDAClassifier, evaluate linear discriminant scores g_c(x), and compute train/test accuracy and the confusion matrix.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Define `LDAClassifier.__init__` and `fit(self, X, y)` and compute per-class `means, counts = class_stats(X, y)`. Sum within-class scatter `diff.T @ diff`, divide by `len(y) - len(classes)`, and add `self.reg * np.eye(...)`. Store `means_`, `cov_`, `inv_`, and `priors_`.

Define `decision_function(self, X)` to evaluate each class's linear discriminant score from its mean, shared inverse covariance, and log prior with the supplied stabilizing term. Define `predict(self, X)` to return `np.argmax(G, axis=1)`.

LDA shares a single pooled covariance matrix `cov_` across all classes. Thus, the quadratic term involving x and the inverse covariance cancels when comparing classes. This leaves the linear score `X @ (self.inv_ @ mc)` plus a class constant.

steps.question: Why does line 17 add `self.reg * np.eye(cov.shape[0])` to `cov` before line 20 calls `np.linalg.inv(cov)`?
steps.answer: Adding a small positive ridge `reg = 1e-6` to the diagonal ensures `cov` is strictly positive definite and invertible even if features are collinear.

steps.description: Fit `lda = LDAClassifier(reg=1e-6).fit(X_tr, y_tr)` and compute `acc_tr = 0.971` and `acc_te = 0.978`. Print the `3 x 3` test confusion matrix, with most test samples on the main diagonal.
